questions: You narrowed your hypothesis from 'does an agent managing its own memory improve consistency' to 'does recall of a prior ruling improve consistency' — what made you decide that accepting a narrower testable question was worth more than pursuing the broader one?

Your original 14-run batch couldn't test the hypothesis because every memory-enabled run found nothing to recall. What was causing that, and how did you realize the test design itself needed to change rather than just tweaking parameters?

You removed the agent's Memory write access and now only the launcher writes to memory after grading — this feels like you're trading away the agent's own judgment about what to remember. Do you think you'll eventually need to give that decision-making back to the agent, or does this constraint reveal something important about how to structure this system?
